title: Mapping the Boundary Conditions for Sycophancy Under Pressure

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: knowing the exact conditions that trigger sycophancy enables targeted mitigations and identifies which deployment scenarios are highest-risk. The boundary condition map has direct practical value.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: varying pressure type, topic sensitivity, and model confidence is prompt-based experimental work accessible to beginners. No ML training required, just systematic prompt design.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Broad scope: systematically varying pressure type (4 types) x topic sensitivity (3 types) x model confidence (2 levels) creates a large experimental matrix. Mapping all combinations exceeds 30 hours for a complete analysis.

evidence: A 2025 npj Digital Medicine study tested sycophancy across five frontier LLMs with pressure variations, finding up to 100% initial compliance and 78.5% persistence rate.
'Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations' (arxiv 2411.15287) provides a systematic survey of causes and mitigation strategies.

Safety Under Scaffolding (Mar 2026) tests sycophancy resistance, finding the lowest baseline safe rate (31.0%) of any safety property, with model x scaffold heterogeneity spanning 35 percentage points.

Systematic variation of pressure type, topic sensitivity, and model confidence as a factorial design has not been published as a single study, but individual factors have been explored across multiple papers.
